results.primary_cause: Evidence is conflicting: reports describe stronger Capesize rates and demand during 2026, while BIMCO-related reporting says the apparent strength was substantially driven by forced rerouting and may reverse as a supply glut develops. The evidence does not establish a durable commodity-volume dry-bulk cycle.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key measure of bulk-shipping rates reached its highest level since December 2023, attributed to rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial, driven by forced rerouting, and that a 2027 supply glut could reverse the benefit.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry Bulk Shipping Faces 2027 Supply Glut: BIMCO Warns Hormuz Rerouting Boost Will Reverse

results.primary_cause: Current evidence indicates storage demand and NAND-related activity, but it does not provide sufficiently precise, time-consistent confirmation of NAND pricing, controller/module demand, or inventory normalization. The available material is also not sufficiently independent for a confident causal classification.

supporting_evidence.claim: A 2026 storage and memory conference report described continued market growth and highlighted AI-driven demand for memory and storage.
supporting_evidence.source_title: 2026 FMS Shows Storage And Memory Market Continued Growth

counter_evidence.claim: A storage-industry analysis argued that NAND supply may not be able to catch demand in the same way as prior cycles, implying structural changes rather than a clearly established conventional pricing and inventory cycle.
counter_evidence.source_title: The Next NAND Decade: Why Supply Can’t Catch Demand The Way It Used To
